rows.title: Freelancer GTM Engineer / AI Automation Specialist (n8n & Clay)
rows.comp: EUR 10,000 fixed for the project build, plus EUR 1,000-5,000 budget for tools/APIs
rows.why: The scope is exactly what he did at FlowSpace and in his GTM/outbound automation work: build a self-hosted n8n stack with Clay waterfall enrichment and Claygent, wired into a CRM with Claude/GPT in the loop. n8n plus lead-enrichment plus CRM integration are all named tools on his CV rather than adjacent ones, and it is a defined-scope freelance build with a disclosed fee — his normal working mode.
rows.watch_outs: Whole job description is written in German and the client is a German solo operator ('Remote (Deutschland)') — confirm the working language before investing time, since German is a hard gate for him. Original post date is April 2026 and the stated delivery window (June-November 2026) has already begun, so part of the scope may be gone; the listing was refreshed and showed 'updated 2 hours ago' at fetch time. EUR 10k for a ~6-month build is modest — worth scoping hours before agreeing. Fee is a fixed project price, not a day rate.

rows.title: Contract Senior Front End Engineer
rows.comp: not disclosed (determined by experience, projects and geographic location)
rows.why: One of the few contract engineering roles found with an unambiguous global eligibility line — 'open to applicants located anywhere around the globe' — so his Italian base and Partita IVA are a non-issue. Next.js/React and Tailwind are his day-to-day stack, and the posting explicitly values strategic use of AI tooling, which is where his agent and automation work differentiates him from a plain front-end contractor.
rows.watch_outs: US company (New York product studio) engaging contractors internationally; posting names no employer-of-record and is not US-payroll-only, so expect to invoice directly — W-8BEN and Partita IVA invoicing on his side. Heavy WordPress block-theme/Gutenberg component of the work that is not on his CV. Agency delivery model means client-driven deadlines and possible US-hours overlap. No rate disclosed and no posted date on the page.

rows.title: Freelance Full-Stack Web App Developer
rows.comp: up to USD 35/hour, depending on level and pace of contribution
rows.why: The requirement line is 'at least 3 years of relevant experience in full-stack web development' with English at B2 — precisely his band, and one of very few contract listings in this sweep that both discloses an hourly rate and is open worldwide. Stack asked for is TypeScript/Node/React/Next.js/PostgreSQL with LLM API integration preferred, which maps onto his FlowSpace migration work and his OpenAI/Eden AI integrations.
rows.watch_outs: Mindrift is an AI-training project platform (Toloka group), so the work is building web apps as training/evaluation material rather than shipping a product to end users — closer to expert gig work than a named client engagement, and weaker CV material than an equivalent product contract. Part-time and project-allocated, so income is not guaranteed once onboarded. USD 35/hour is a ceiling, not a floor. Paid in USD — invoice via Partita IVA and expect Wise/Deel-style rails.

rows.title: Contract Senior Web Engineer
rows.comp: not disclosed (determined by experience, projects and geographic location)
rows.why: Same global contract terms as Fueled's front-end role and the only posting in this sweep whose stated requirement — '2+ years in a consulting/agency environment' — is a direct match for how his career actually reads: eight European companies, coordinating an external agency, mediating between client and delivery team. Modern PHP plus React overlaps his Laravel and Next.js experience, and it is flagged contract-with-potential-transition-to-full-time.
rows.watch_outs: Core of the role is enterprise-scale WordPress and Gutenberg block development, which he cannot evidence — the weakest stack match of the four rows, and the PHP overlap is Laravel rather than WordPress. Same US-studio contracting logistics as the front-end role (direct invoicing, W-8BEN, no EOR mentioned). No rate and no posted date disclosed. Applying to both Fueled contract roles at once may read as unfocused — pick the front-end one first.
